content.title: About
content.content: Russet potatoes are a large, russet‑skinned variety with a yellowish flesh that is commonly sold without skin. Raw, unpeeled russet potatoes are high in starch, B‑vitamins, vitamin C, and potassium. They are used in cooking for mashed potatoes, casseroles, and salads after heat treatment.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Russet is one of the most popular potato varieties in the United States, known for its versatility.
Skinless potatoes are often used in the food industry for frozen product manufacturing.
Russet potatoes contain more starch than most other varieties, making them ideal for smooth mash.
Raw potatoes contain solanine, a toxin that is destroyed by cooking.
Russet potatoes have relatively low sugar content, reducing the risk of acrylamide formation when fried.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal heart function, muscle contraction, and nerve signaling.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant and helps strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Raw potatoes contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Solanine
items.content: Raw potatoes may contain solanine, which is toxic in large amounts. Proper cooking eliminates the risk.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: High glycemic index after cooking
items.content: Cooking raises the glycemic index, which can affect blood sugar levels in people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw skinless potatoes are rarely eaten raw; they are typically boiled, baked, or fried first. After cooking they can be used in mashed potatoes, salads, soups, and casseroles. Since the skin is already removed, there is no need to peel before preparation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store potatoes in a cool, dark, dry place at 4‑10 °C. Keep humidity low to prevent sprouting and rot. For longer storage, place them in paper bags rather than plastic.
